concepts.title: Sensing and Responding to the Environment

questions.q: How do animals sense and respond to their surroundings?
questions.a: Through sense organs and nervous or hormonal systems - dogs hear better, we react to hot stoves instantly.

questions.q: How do plants respond to the environment without nerves?
questions.a: By slow growth movements (toward light) and quick turgor changes (mimosa leaves).

questions.q: Give one example of an animal responding to danger.
questions.a: A deer flees on hearing a sound; a snail pulls into its shell when touched.

questions.q: What is a population in ecology?
questions.a: All the members of one species living in an area - e.g. all deer of a forest.
Different populations of plants and animals living together in one area.

questions.q: How are populations and communities linked to an ecosystem?
questions.a: Communities plus their physical surroundings work together as an ecosystem.

questions.q: Give one example each of cooperation and competition among organisms.
questions.a: Cooperation: ants working in a colony. Competition: lions and hyenas hunting the same prey.
One organism killing and eating another - the predator-prey link keeps populations in check.

questions.q: How do parasites differ from predators?
questions.a: Parasites live on/in a host and take food slowly without killing at once; predators kill their prey.
A line of who eats whom - grass -> deer -> tiger - passing energy from producers to consumers.
Many linked food chains in an ecosystem, since most animals eat several foods.

questions.q: Why can food chains not go on forever?
questions.a: Only 10% of energy passes to each level, so after 3-4 links too little energy remains.

concepts.title: Decomposers and the Balance of Nature

questions.a: They break down dead plants, animals and waste into simple soil nutrients.

questions.q: What would happen if decomposers vanished?
questions.a: Dead matter would pile up, nutrients would not return to soil, and life would slowly fail.
All living things of an area together with their non-living surroundings, interacting as one system.

questions.q: Name two natural and two man-made ecosystems.
questions.a: Natural: forest, pond. Man-made: aquarium, crop field.
They give food, water, oxygen, timber, medicines and regulate climate and floods.
